title: Sampling & ethics
examples: What is the difference between random and convenience sampling?
Can you explain the ethical guidelines researchers must follow?
When is it okay to use deception in a psychology study?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how to choose groups for studies. We are also looking at ethical rules for research.

items: Sampling methods help us choose participants.
Ethics guide how research must be done.

explain.say: One method is random sampling. This means every person has an equal chance of being picked.
Another type is convenience sampling. This uses people who are easy for the researcher to reach.
Ethically, researchers must get informed consent first. This means participants know what they are joining.
Confidentiality is also key. Researchers must keep all personal information secret from others.
In real life, imagine a school survey about stress. Using convenience sampling might only include students who visit the library.

faq.q: What is the main difference between random and convenience sampling?
faq.a: Random sampling ensures everyone has an equal chance of being chosen, which is better for generalisation. You could also ask if it is representative or if it only uses available people.
asks: How do I make sure my sample is fair?

faq.q: Why must researchers get informed consent before a study?
faq.a: Informed consent respects the participant's autonomy by ensuring they fully understand the risks and benefits. Other ways to ask this are: 'Do people have to agree to take part?' or 'What is the right to withdraw?'
asks: What if they change their mind?

faq.q: What does confidentiality mean in research terms?
faq.a: Confidentiality means that the researcher promises not to share any identifying details about the participants. You might also hear this described as keeping data private or anonymising results.
asks: Will my name be attached to my answers?
Can you promise not to tell anyone?

faq.q: Can researchers ever use deception in a study?
faq.a: Deception is only allowed if it is absolutely necessary and if participants are fully debriefed afterwards. This means they must be told the truth immediately after the session.

faq.q: What is the ethical guideline regarding vulnerable populations?
faq.a: Researchers must take extra care with vulnerable groups, like children or people with certain conditions. This means extra safeguards must be put in place for them.
asks: Who needs special protection in research?

facts: Random sampling aims to create a sample that mirrors the larger population.
Informed consent requires participants to understand the procedures and risks.
Confidentiality protects the identity of the participants even if the data is shared.
Researchers must debrief participants if deception was used.

quiz.say: A study on local teenagers only surveys students from one specific high school. Which sampling method is this?
quiz.why: This method uses people who are easily accessible to the researcher.

wrong.1: This requires a list of every student in the area, not just one school.
wrong.2: This method requires dividing the population into groups first.
wrong.3: This involves picking every nth person from a list, which is more structured.

quiz.say: A researcher tells participants they are studying memory, but they are actually testing honesty. What ethical procedure must happen immediately after?
quiz.why: Debriefing is necessary to explain the true purpose of the study after deception.

wrong.0: Minimising risk is a continuous process, not a single step after deception.
wrong.2: Consent happens before the study starts, not after.
wrong.3: Anonymity is about keeping names secret, not revealing the true purpose.

quiz.say: If a researcher uses a list of all registered voters in a city to pick names for a study, what is the best sampling method?
quiz.why: Having a complete list allows every person an equal chance of selection.

wrong.0: This only includes people who choose to participate willingly.
wrong.2: This would only use people the researcher happens to meet.
wrong.3: While possible, random sampling is the most robust method when a full list exists.
